segments.text: Today, we're diving into the top 18 trending AI projects on GitHub. All ready for you to clone and experiment
with right now. These repos will supercharge your workflow, inspire your next side project, and maybe even change
the game. So, hit that star button and let's explore the world of AI together.
First up, SecondMe is an open-source experiment in digital individuality trained locally, owned fully by you, and
connected to a global network of AI identities. It's built around a bold idea. Instead of building a single super
AI, what if everyone could train their own? You can teach your second Mi who you are using hierarchical memory modeling and a mi alignment algorithm
that captures your tone, your context, and your reasoning. run it locally for full privacy or scale it up across a
decentralized network to interact with other AI selves. What if building reliable LM applications had a playbook
like the 12 Factor app for AI? 12FA agents lays down the principles for building production grade AI agents, not
just looping LLM toys, but real software you can put in front of customers. The creator tested every framework, Langchain, Crew Aai, Langraph, you name
it, and realized most so-called agents are just regular programs with a few LLM calls sprinkled in. So, this project
goes deeper, distilling the hard-earned lessons from hundreds of founders into 12 core principles for serious AI systems.
Video diffusion is finally becoming practical, and it's all thanks to Frame Pack. This open- source project brings a breakthrough in next frame prediction
models, letting AI generate videos progressively, just like image diffusion. Frame pack introduces frame
context packing, a clever trick that compresses all previous frames into a fixed length context, meaning no matter
how long your video gets, the workload stays the same. That means you can train and run highquality video models, even
massive 13B parameter ones, right on your laptop GPU.
Meet Prompt Optimizer, your AI prompt co-pilot that helps you write smarter, sharper, and more effective prompts for
any model. Whether you're fine-tuning small local models or optimizing production level systems, this open- source tool takes prompt engineering
from guesswork to science. It offers four ways to use it. Web, desktop, Chrome extension, and even Docker, so you can fit it right into your workflow.
Behind the scenes, Prompt Optimizer runs multi-round iterative improvements to fine-tune your text, compare versions
side by side, and instantly show how optimization changes the model's response.
Turning messy text into structured, verifiable data. That's the magic of Lang Extract. It's a Python library that
uses LLMs to extract information from unstructured documents like reports, logs, or clinical notes and map every
piece of data exactly to where it came from in the source text. That means every extraction is grounded, traceable, and auditable. You can literally
highlight and verify each field in context. Lang Extract enforces a consistent schema through few examples and controlled generation. So your
output isn't just AI guesswork. It's structured, reliable data ready for production.
What if you could turn clawed code into a full-blown AI development platform?
That's exactly what the SuperCloud framework does. It's a meta programming and orchestration system that supercharges Claude with intelligent
agents, workflow automation, and structured development tools, transforming prompts into full project
pipelines. version 4 with 16 specialized agents, a PM agent that documents as it learns, a security engineer that catches
real vulnerabilities, a front-end architect that knows your UI patterns, all working together automatically.
Agent to agent protocol or A2A is an open standard that lets AI agents built on completely different frameworks, even
running on separate servers, talk to each other securely and intelligently.
Think of it as the common language for autonomous systems, enabling agents to discover each other's capabilities, negotiate how they'll interact, and work
together on longunning tasks, all without exposing their private memory or internal logic. It's like APIs for AI
personalities, connecting specialized agents so they can team up on problems no single agent could solve alone.
What happens when you turn a trading floor into a team of AI agents?
Trading Agents is a multi-agent LLM framework that simulates the structure of a real trading firm, complete with analysts, researchers, traders, and risk
managers, all collaborating to make market decisions. Each agent has a specialty. The fundamentals analyst studies company performance. The sentiment analyst tracks public mood.
The news analyst monitors global events.
And the technical analyst reads the charts. Their insights flow into a research debate where bullish and bearish agents argue strategy and the
trader agent synthesizes it all into actionable decisions.
Meet Open Code, the open- source AI coding agent built for developers who live in the command line. It's runs natively in your terminal and gives you
total freedom. Any provider, any model, any editor. The interface, a sleek,
responsive TUI that automatically loads the right language servers for your project. You can start multiple agent sessions in parallel, share debugging
links with your team, and even log in with your Claude Pro or Max account with over 29,000 GitHub stars and 200,000 devs using it every month.
Next up, Claude Code Plugins.
Intelligent automation and multi-agent orchestration for developers. This system brings together 85 specialized AI
agents, 15 workflow orchestrators, 47 modular skills, and 44 development tools. All organized into 63 focused
single-purpose plugins built specifically for cloud code. Each plugin is lightweight, isolated, and composable, so you only load what you
need, keeping token usage low and efficiency high. Whether you're automating full stack builds, securing your infrastructure, or running ML
pipelines, Claude Code Plugins gives you a complete multi- aent toolkit.
Meet Kronos, a foundation model built for the language of financial markets.
Unlike generalpurpose time series models, Kronos is trained specifically on candlestick or kine data from over 45
global exchanges, capturing the patterns and nuances of high-noise financial markets. It's a decoderonly transformer
model with a two-stage framework. First, a specialized tokenizer converts continuous OLCV data into hierarchical
discrete tokens. Then, a large auto reggressive transformer learns these sequences, enabling Kronos to perform a
variety of quantitative tasks from pattern recognition to predictive modeling.
Introducing Krillin AI, the minimalist powerhouse for AI video translation and dubbing. Whether you're localizing YouTube content or repurposing short
form clips for platforms like Tik Tok, Billilly or WeChat video, Krillin AI gives you a seamless end-to-end workflow
from raw footage to fully dubbed crossplatform video with one-click setup. It installs everything automatically. No complex environment
needed. It supports YTDLP downloads, local uploads, whisper-based transcription, LLM powered translation
and segmentation, and even voice cloning through cozy voice or your own custom voice.
Meet Cloudflow, the enterprise AI orchestration platform redefining how intelligent systems think, collaborate,
and build. Cloudflow lets you deploy autonomous multi-agent swarms that coordinate, reason, and evolve. powered
by persistent memory and over 100 advanced MCP tools. With 25 natural language cla, semantic vector search,
and a queen-led swarm architecture, your agents don't just execute tasks, they orchestrate entire development life
cycles. From GitHub automation to rag enhanced reasoning, Claude Flow brings together speed, structure, and swarm intelligence.
backend chaos. APIs here, jobs there, agents everywhere. Mochia changes that.
It's a multi- language back-end framework that unifies APIs, background jobs, workflows, cues, and even AI
agents, all into a single elegant primitive called the step. Think of it like what React did for the front end, but for your back end. With steps, every
part of your system from endpoints to event streams follows the same pattern, the same life cycle, the same mental model. No more juggling half a dozen
frameworks for scheduling, observability, or state management. MOSHA bakes it all in seamlessly.
Meet Easy Data Set, the tool for creating highquality fine-tuning data sets for large language models. Upload
your domain files, PDFs, Markdown, DOCX, and Easy Data Set does the heavy lifting. It splits text intelligently,
extracts key ideas, and even generates questions and answers automatically, complete with chain of thought reasoning. You can edit every step,
assign domain labels, and export your data set in formats like alpaca, share GPT, or multilingual JSON. All ready for
OpenAI compatible APIs. Think of it as your personal data engineer and prompt designer in one. Built with an interface anyone can use.
Ever wish your AI coding agent could just understand your Figma design? Like actually read it instead of guessing
from screenshots? Introducing Framelink MCP for Figma, the bridge between your design files and your coding agents like
cursor. With Framelink, your AI doesn't just see pixels. It reads real layout, styles, and hierarchy data directly from Figma through the model context
protocol. That means no more messy screenshot hacks. Your AI can now implement designs accurately in one shot
across any framework. Just drop a Figma link in your IDE chat and your agent fetches everything it needs to write pixel perfect code.
Tiny zero is a tiny minimal reproduction of DeepSeeks R10 that makes that aha moment cheap and visible. Think emergent
self-verification, search, and iterative revision from a 3B model for under $30.
The idea is simple. Give a base LM prompts and a groundtruth reward. Run reinforcement learning and let the model
discover tactics. Applied to tasks like countdown and number multiplication, Tiny Zero shows the model inventing
search strategies, proposing solutions, checking them, and then revising until it works.
Imagine telling Claude to build your 3D scene, and watching Blender do it live.
Blender MCP bridges Blender and Claude AI using the model context protocol, giving Claude direct access to manipulate your 3D world. It's like
giving your AI a pair of hands inside Blender. With Blender MCP, you can create, modify, and delete 3D objects on
command. Apply realistic materials, tweak colors, and adjust lighting.
Inspect entire scenes, and get structured reports on every object. even run Python code in Blender straight from Claude.
